requirements.text: One versioned routing policy owns workflow route, model, effort, rollout, override, and capability semantics.
Classification and provider execution remain separate; Quick Dev may decide a class but cannot schedule a provider.
Quick Dev deterministically selects small_mechanical, normal, complex, or architectural by highest matching typed trigger.
VDD reuses standard, resumable, and self-hosted profile selection and uses max only for a typed, capability-gated complex recovery escalation.
Refactor Acceptance remains deterministic except for a closed complex-recovery route; Bootstrap model authority cannot be overridden.
The shared launcher uses UTF-8 stdin, shell-free invocation, explicit sandbox and model identity, and no hidden fallback.
Every decision records typed inputs, triggers, policy revision, requested route, override, capability state, and requested versus actual execution identity with authorizes empty.
User upgrades are allowed; downgrades cannot clear protected, architectural, or unresolved-boundary triggers.
Luna and Sol/max remain inactive until exact-surface capability probes and representative shadow predicates pass.
Rollout is backward-compatible, observe-only first, independently disableable by consumer, and preserves historical evidence.

acceptance.assertion: A schema-valid registry covers every active consumer route with full model IDs and supported effort values.
Unknown routes, short runtime aliases, and duplicate policy ownership fail closed.
Tests prove the Quick Dev adapter emits decisions but the shared launcher alone invokes run_llm_exec.
Table-driven tests cover all four Quick Dev classes and highest-match precedence.
Every architectural trigger routes to architectural even when mechanical facts are also present.
Unknown or contradictory facts never route to small_mechanical.
VDD profile mapping is stable and max requires a typed recovery trigger plus a passing capability probe.
Ordinary Acceptance actions execute no model process.
Bootstrap profile, round, verifier, effort, and access-proof decisions byte-match Bootstrap authority and reject router overrides.
Shared backend tests cover explicit model and all policy-supported reasoning efforts.
Launcher tests prove stdin transport, shell-free execution, sandbox binding, no secret persistence, and no automatic fallback loop.
Decision and execution evidence is schema-valid, hash-bound, redacted, non-authorizing, and records requested versus actual identity.
Upgrade overrides pass and unsafe downgrade overrides fail with stable reason codes.
A failed or unavailable exact-model probe leaves the route disabled without substituting another model.
Shadow evaluation compares task predicates and reports quality, latency, and cost without granting activation authority.
Observe-only mode changes no current-session model and launches no child process.
Each consumer can be disabled independently and existing VDD, Quick Dev, Acceptance, and Bootstrap tests remain green.

slices.title: Decision and policy kernel
slices.recovery: Remove the new inactive policy and ADR changes; no caller behavior is enabled.

slices.title: Shared launcher and capability boundary
slices.recovery: Set rollout to observe_only and retain non-authorizing decisions.

slices.title: Quick Dev four-class router
slices.recovery: Disable the quick-dev consumer and continue using the caller session model.

slices.title: VDD and Acceptance consumers
slices.recovery: Disable VDD and Acceptance consumers independently; preserve historical runs.

slices.title: Shadow evaluation, migration, and terminal replay
slices.recovery: Keep observe_only and defer activation while preserving logs.
